# ampr-ripd

**Keeps a gateway's routes current on the amateur radio IP network**

- **Version recorded:** 2.4.1
- **Categories:** `packet-nodes`
- **Upstream:** <http://www.yo2loj.ro/hamprojects/>

## What it does

Listens for the RIPv2 routing announcements the AMPRnet gateway system broadcasts and installs the resulting routes and tunnel endpoints into the kernel, so a station on the 44.0.0.0/8 amateur network reaches the rest of it without hand-maintained routing.

## Why you would want it

AMPRnet is a real IP network allocated to amateur radio, reached over IP-IP tunnels between gateways whose addresses change. Maintaining those routes by hand is not practical; this is the daemon that does it, and it is what turns a 44-net allocation into working connectivity.

## Before it will work

An AMPRnet allocation and a registered gateway, which are administrative steps rather than software ones. Kernel IP-IP tunnelling. The Blend marks this as a Suggests rather than a Recommends precisely because it is only useful to gateway operators.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`packet`](../profiles/packet.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install ampr-ripd --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `ampr-ripd`

## Known problems

Only useful if you run a gateway; on an ordinary station it will run and do nothing visible. It installs kernel routes, so a misconfiguration affects the whole machine's networking rather than one application. AMPRnet address space has been partly reallocated in recent years and some documentation found online predates that.
